page.headline: Does xs still beat rsync when neo has two CPUs?
page.intro: The lab is checking whether xs -a -j4 keeps its speed advantage over rsync -a when neo is limited to 2 CPUs, and whether the real-projects gap seen in lab2 reproduces. The neo runner handles network pulls to mars over an 11 ms link, while neo-ssd runs local copies to the Samsung T5 with the same CPU cap. Each runner works through its queue in order, starting with the real-psample checks.

items.asks: For lab2's real-projects fresh gap: on a fresh real-psample copy into a 2-CPU arm64 receiver behind 11 ms, is xs -a -j4 slower than rsync -a, or does it show a block-to-block stall like lab2's 8.8 to 98 s spread?
items.hypothesis: With neo receiving under 11 ms and 2 CPUs, xs -a -j4's time-to-durable is at least 5% behind rsync -a, or its per-block times vary far more than rsync's.
items.why: Runs now to test whether lab2's real-psample gap comes from a slower time-to-durable on a fresh copy or from block-to-block stalls behind 11 ms.

items.asks: For lab2's real-projects fresh gap: on the plain neo-mars link, with no added latency and no CPU cap, how does xs -a -j4 compare with rsync -a on a fresh real-psample copy?
items.hypothesis: On the plain link, xs -a -j4 copies real-psample fresh no slower than rsync -a, so any loss in L2R3 comes from lab2's conditions.
items.why: Runs next to set a plain-link baseline, so any loss seen under lab2's conditions can be attributed to latency and CPU limits rather than to xs itself.

items.asks: Before lab2 measures them: does xs -a -j4 still beat rsync -a on fresh and no-op copies of small-flat, small-deep and mixed-bimodal into a 2-CPU arm64 receiver behind 11 ms?
items.hypothesis: In at least one of these six cells, rsync -a's time-to-durable comes within 5% of xs -a -j4's or beats it, since its plain-link lead there was 1.1x to 3x.
items.why: Checks whether xs still beats rsync on small and mixed copies under 2 CPUs and 11 ms, where rsync led by 1.1x to 3x on the plain link.

items.asks: In lab2's direction (2-CPU sender, 11 ms), does xs -a -j4 still beat rsync -a when re-syncing real-congress at a no-op and after a 1% change?
items.hypothesis: Under 11 ms and a 2-CPU sender, xs -a -j4 stays at least 5% faster than rsync -a at both the no-op and the 1% update of real-congress.
items.why: Tests whether xs stays at least 5% faster than rsync when re-syncing real-congress under 11 ms with a 2-CPU sender, at a no-op and after a 1% change.

items.asks: For lab2's real-projects fresh gap: copying real-psample locally to the T5 with cold caches and neo held to 2 CPUs, does xs -a -j4's existing deficit to rsync -a (about 10% in LC1 and LC12) widen?
items.hypothesis: With 2 CPUs, xs -a -j4 is more than 15% slower than rsync -a on a fresh cold local real-psample copy, which would point at CPU contention among its workers.
items.why: Tests whether a 2-CPU cap widens xs's existing local deficit on a cold real-psample copy to the T5, which would point at contention among its workers.

items.asks: With neo held to 2 CPUs, as lab2's sender is, does xs -a -j4 keep its local lead over rsync -a on real-congress no-op and update re-syncs?
items.hypothesis: Under a 2-CPU cap, rsync -a's time-to-durable comes within 5% of xs -a -j4's in at least one of the no-op, 0.1%, 1% and 10% update cells, where xs's plain-link no-op lead was 4.7x (J2).
items.why: Checks whether xs keeps its local lead over rsync on real-congress re-syncs with neo capped at 2 CPUs, matching lab2's sender conditions.

items.asks: With neo held to 2 CPUs, does xs -a -j4 still beat rsync -a on local fresh and no-op copies of small-flat, small-deep and mixed-bimodal?
items.hypothesis: Under a 2-CPU cap, xs -a -j4's lead over rsync -a shrinks below 5% in at least one of these six cells, from 1.25x to 4.8x on the plain link (J2).
items.why: Tests whether the 2-CPU cap pushes xs's local lead below 5% on small-flat, small-deep and mixed-bimodal copies, where the plain-link lead was 1.25x to 4.8x.

items.asks: For the corpus behind lab2's real-projects gap: with neo held to 2 CPUs, does xs -a -j4 still re-sync real-psample faster than rsync -a at a no-op and after a 1% change?
items.hypothesis: Under a 2-CPU cap, xs -a -j4 stays at least 5% faster than rsync -a at the real-psample no-op, as on the plain link (about 0.5x, LC4), but its lead at the 1% update is under 5%.
items.why: Checks the corpus behind lab2's real-projects gap, asking whether xs still re-syncs real-psample at least 5% faster at a no-op and whether its 1% lead has shrunk.
